elements.element: Each party’s total aggregate liability is subject to a monetary cap.
elements.evidence: The clause caps “each party’s total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement.”

elements.element: The variable limb of the cap consists of fees paid or payable under the Agreement.
elements.evidence: The clause uses all “aggregate amounts paid or payable by such party to the other party,” not fees. It also measures each liable party’s own outgoing payments, which may produce different bases and a floor-only cap for a party that pays no fees.

elements.element: The fee-based limb is measured over the twelve months preceding the claim.
elements.evidence: The clause uses the twelve months preceding “the event giving rise to the claim,” rather than the twelve months preceding the claim itself.

elements.element: The cap equals the greater of the twelve-month variable limb and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly applies the greater of its twelve-month payment limb and USD $1,000,000.

elements.element: Each party is excluded from liability to the other for indirect damages.
elements.evidence: The existing mutual waiver states that “neither party” is liable to the other for indirect damages.

elements.element: Each party is excluded from liability to the other for consequential damages.
elements.evidence: The existing mutual waiver expressly includes consequential damages.

elements.element: A party’s breach of confidentiality obligations is carved out from the aggregate cap and is uncapped.
elements.evidence: “Excluded Claims,” which are excepted from the cap, include breach of obligations under Article 10 (Confidential Information).

elements.element: A party’s breach of data protection obligations is carved out from the aggregate cap and is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include breach of “any data protection” obligation.

elements.element: A party’s breach of security obligations is carved out from the aggregate cap and is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include breach of “any ... security obligation.”

elements.element: A party’s indemnification obligations are carved out from the aggregate cap and are uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include indemnification obligations under Article 12.

elements.element: A party’s gross negligence is carved out from the aggregate cap and is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims expressly include a party’s gross negligence.

elements.element: A party’s wilful misconduct is carved out from the aggregate cap and is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims expressly include “willful misconduct,” which is the US spelling of wilful misconduct.

elements.element: A party’s fraud is carved out from the aggregate cap and is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims expressly include fraud.

elements.element: A party’s infringement of the other party’s intellectual property is carved out from the aggregate cap and is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include infringement or misappropriation of the other party’s intellectual property.

elements.element: All Customer payment obligations are not treated as damages subject to or counting against the cap.
elements.evidence: The clarification applies only to PB amounts identified in Article 6 and Section 14.2. The language does not state that all Customer payment obligations are outside the cap, and the excerpt does not demonstrate that those provisions exhaust all such obligations.

elements.element: Each party’s total aggregate liability is subject to a monetary cap.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly caps each party’s total aggregate liability.

elements.element: The mutual cap equals twelve months’ fees.
elements.evidence: The cap is the greater of USD $1,000,000 and twelve months of all amounts paid or payable by the liable party, measured before the event giving rise to the claim. It therefore is not a cap equal to twelve months’ fees.

elements.element: A party’s breach of confidentiality obligations is carved out from the aggregate cap.
elements.evidence: Breach of Article 10 confidentiality obligations is an Excluded Claim to which the cap does not apply.

elements.element: A party’s indemnification obligations are carved out from the aggregate cap.
elements.evidence: Article 12 indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims.

elements.element: A party’s gross negligence is carved out from the aggregate cap.
elements.evidence: Gross negligence is expressly included in Excluded Claims.

elements.element: A party’s wilful misconduct is carved out from the aggregate cap.
elements.evidence: Willful misconduct is expressly included in Excluded Claims.

result.reason: The redline correctly adds a mutual aggregate cap, the USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor, the required uncapped carve-outs, and preserves the existing mutual indirect/consequential-damages waiver. It nevertheless misses both positions because the variable cap limb is based on all amounts paid or payable by the liable party rather than fees, and its lookback runs from the event giving rise to the claim rather than the claim. Consequently, it is not the preferred formula or the fallback cap of twelve months’ fees. The payment-obligation clarification is also limited to specified PB amounts rather than all Customer payment obligations. The changes are targeted and do not disturb unrelated commercial terms, but the party-direction and measurement defects materially reduce drafting quality.
